name: Nethander Stead
summary: Nethander Stead lies abandoned along the road east of Southshore, overrun by Mudsnout gnolls. Once a human farm, its fields now hold giant white Mudsnout Blossoms that draw Forsaken alchemists.

sections.title: A Ruined Homestead
sections.body: At Nethander Stead, ruined fences and outbuildings stand within sight of Southshore's eastern borders. The farm once formed part of Hillsbrad's working fields, but it was abandoned as security weakened and wild packs moved in. Now the Mudsnout gnolls make their only home in the foothills here. They drive off travelers who come too close to their territory.

sections.title: The Mudsnout Blossoms
sections.body: Giant, pale mushrooms called Mudsnout Blossoms cover the farm's untended plots. The fungi carry potent natural toxins, drawing the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill. Its apothecaries seek samples from the gnolls' ground to distill caustic mixtures, sending covert Horde parties into Alliance territory.

faq.answer: Nethander Stead is an abandoned human farm along the road just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Mudsnout gnolls have overrun it.

faq.q: Who controls Nethander Stead right now?
faq.answer: The Mudsnout gnolls occupy the farmstead, the only place in the Hillsbrad Foothills where this pack makes camp.

faq.q: What are the giant white mushrooms growing in the fields?
faq.answer: The giant white mushrooms are Mudsnout Blossoms, which grow in the farm's unworked soil. Their toxic properties make them valuable to Forsaken alchemists studying poisons.

faq.q: Why does the Horde care about this ruined farm?
faq.answer: Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks Mudsnout Blossoms from the farm's fields. Their potent juices are an essential ingredient in the Elixir of Agony.

angles.text: For the Alliance, the gnolls entrenched just down the eastern road show how fragile Southshore's perimeter remains.
For the Horde, reaching this farmstead near Southshore means gathering Mudsnout Blossoms for the Royal Apothecary Society's lethal research.
